primitives.name: Sentiment Labeling Protocol
primitives.verbatim_quote: Dataset / schema Twitter messages labeled by 5 Mechanical Turk annotators each; annotators required >95% approval rating and ≥50 approved HITs; $0.03 per HIT.
primitives.assumptions: Annotator agreement produces stable gold labels; human judgment is consistent across tasks.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when annotator pool lacks quality control or consensus fails.

layer2.mapping: GSE adopts identical labeling protocol for sports-text sentiment benchmarks.

primitives.name: F1 Macro-Average Metric
primitives.verbatim_quote: Equations & assumptions Metric: F = (F_positive + F_negative)/2, i.e., macro-average of F1 over the two polar classes (neutral excluded).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F': 'F1-score (dimensionless)', 'F_{\\text{pos}}': 'F1 for positive class', 'F_{\\text{neg}}': 'F1 for negative class'}
primitives.assumptions: Positive and negative classes are equally weighted; neutral class is excluded from scoring.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when class imbalance skews macro-average toward dominant class.

layer2.mapping: GSE uses (F_pos + F_neg)/2 for bullish/bearish classification in sports news.
layer2.telemetry: Macro-F1 score on labeled sports tweets

primitives.name: Phrase vs Message Subtask Split
primitives.verbatim_quote: Two subtasks: (A) phrase-level polarity in context, (B) message-level polarity; two domains: Twitter and SMS.
primitives.assumptions: Contextual sentiment varies between phrase and full message; both domains require distinct modeling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure when subtask boundaries are ambiguous or context ignored.

layer2.mapping: GSE splits sports-text into sentence-level and document-level sentiment tasks.
layer2.telemetry: Performance difference between phrase and message subtasks
